descriptors.R: nominee of the party, organized since 1854 and strongest in the free states, that would bar slavery from every territory; a former one-term congressman and lawyer from the Northwest
descriptors.D: nominee of the Northern wing of the administration party, which split at its convention; a senator from the Northwest who holds that each territory's settlers should decide on slavery for themselves
descriptors.O: nominee of the Southern wing of the divided administration party; the sitting Vice-President, who holds that the federal government must protect slaveholders' property in every territory

compile_desc.R: the party organized since 1854 against the extension of slavery
compile_desc.D: the Northern wing of the divided administration party

others_line: Other candidates on some ballots, including the nominee of a new Union-first party of conservatives from the border states, a former senator (answer "other").
never_name: Lincoln, Hamlin, Douglas, Herschel Johnson, Breckinridge, Lane, Bell, Everett, Buchanan or Seward

slice_sources.men: 1860 census (Eighth Census), white men 21+ outside the eleven later-Confederate states; property tests had mostly ended, and only five New England states let Black men vote on equal terms; calibrated to certified returns.
slice_sources.women: No women could vote for president in 1860; 1860 census women 21+ shown for population only.
slice_sources.south-white: 1860 census, white adults in the eleven later-Confederate states; white men voted except in South Carolina, whose legislature chose its electors; the free-soil nominee was on no ballot in ten of these states; calibrated to certified returns.
slice_sources.black-south: 1860 census, Black adults in the eleven later-Confederate states, overwhelmingly enslaved; enslaved people could not vote and no Southern state let free Black men vote.
slice_sources.immigrants: 1860 census, foreign-born white men not yet naturalized; several Midwestern and Western states let declarant aliens vote, elsewhere only naturalized men could.
